title: Source registry listed 14 of 38 hospital columns
found: first load of the real Hospital General Information file (real data)
detail: The loader's contract for the hospital file listed 14 columns, but the real CMS file has 38. Every first load therefore reported 24 added columns, which would bury a genuine drift alert in noise. The registry now lists all 38 columns, so only a real change is reported.

title: CMS suppression text crashed typed staging
found: profiling the real files, then the first dbt run (real data)
detail: CMS puts text inside numeric columns: N/A for 10,088 discharge counts, Too Few to Report for 3,683 readmission counts, and Not Available for 2,245 star ratings. A plain cast stopped the build. Staging now uses try_cast, so suppressed cells become null and the footnote code keeps the reason.

title: 20 hospitals in HRRP are missing from General Information
detail: The fact table inner-joined the hospital dimension, so readmission rows for 20 hospitals would have disappeared with no error. dim_hospital now keeps those hospitals, flagged in_general_info = false, and a relationships test guards the join.

title: A new CMS condition code was silently dropped from the worklist
found: SIMULATED CMS refresh while reviewing joins; the current real files are not affected
detail: The worklist inner-joined a label seed, so a condition CMS adds in a later refresh would vanish from the work queue. The join is now a left join with an Unlabeled measure fallback, and a singular test reconciles the worklist to the fact table.

title: Governed metric disagreed with the marts
found: review of metric and mart definitions; LATENT, the current real files do not trigger it
detail: The semantic layer measure summed excess readmissions for every pair, while the marts count only pairs with reportable volume (25 or more discharges). With a small hospital that has a published ratio, a self-service user would see a different number than the dashboard. The measure now applies the same rule and a test compares the two.
